child.family_role_pattern: extended family members help with care

parent.family_role_pattern: extended family members help with care

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I'm going to ask you some questions about how you and your family have been. I will ask about several areas. I will ask about how you've felt physically and your feelings. I will ask about school and friends. I will also ask about information about sleep or taking medicine. We will make a summary of your responses to share with your medical team. Your team is your doctors and your nurses. It is also other people who work with you here. I'll just call them your care team. The things you tell us help the care team to know how to help you. If you ever need to share something urgent or that can't wait, make sure you call your care team right away, or have your family help you call.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm good to start.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will start by asking about how you've felt physically. Have you had any problems with pain? What about sleep? What about nausea? What about your energy level?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Nothing much. I sleep fine and I got through a full week of school without sitting anything out.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Now I want to ask about your feelings. Have you felt sad, worried, grumpy, or lonely? Have you felt different from usual?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Mostly annoyed. Everyone at home still handles me like I'm going to break, and I take it out on my mom when she hasn't done anything.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will make a note that you are annoyed with how they treat you at home. How is schoolwork going? Have you been able to stay in touch with your friends? How are those things going?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: School's going, I guess. I get the work back with a grade on it that I can't explain. I'm sitting in the class and I never actually learned the middle part of it.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will make a note that you missed the middle of what your class did. Anything else you want to tell me?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Something else. My mom and my grandmother argue about me every week — my grandmother thinks I should still be resting and my mom says I'm fine. Neither of them asks me.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will make a note that your mom and your grandmother argue about you. Have you had any difficulties with taking medicine, sleeping, eating, or using the bathroom regularly?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I take one tablet at night and nothing else now. They started asking my mom to step outside for part of my appointments when I turned seventeen, and I'd rather she stayed in the room.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Anything else that you would like to share?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's everything from me.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Okay, thanks for sharing all of that information. Now, I will make a summary of topics that may be helpful to discuss with your medical team. I'm going to give everything a number. You can just let me know which numbers are most important. We can make them bold and put them at the top of the list. Okay, here's your list:
1. Being annoyed at everyone at home
2. Schoolwork he is behind on without it showing
3. His mom and his grandmother arguing over him
4. Wanting his mom to stay in the room
Which ones should we put on the top of the list?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Put the school one up, 2. Then 4, my mom staying in the room. Then the arguing at 3.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Here's your list:
1. Schoolwork he is behind on without it showing
2. Wanting his mom to stay in the room
3. His mom and his grandmother arguing over him
4. Being annoyed at everyone at home
Any changes?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yep. I'd keep it like that.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Thanks for talking with me today. I hope your conversation with the medical team will help. Please be sure to talk about these items in more detail with your medical team.
—
If anything urgent comes up between visits, make sure you call your care team right away.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I'm going to ask you some specific questions about how you and your family are doing. I will ask about problems in a number of areas. I will ask about your child's physical health, how you are doing emotionally, family and social things, practical things, and how things are communicated with you and your child. We will share a summary of your responses with the medical team. We hope that this process will help with communication and ensuring access to resources. The medical team is your doctors and your nurses. They can address things and offer referrals and support services as needed. This also gives us information about how these services may be working for you. Then we know what we may need to change. If you ever have urgent or time-sensitive concerns between visits, make sure that you call your care team directly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yes. I've been waiting to be asked some of this.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will start by asking about how your child is doing physically. Have they had any problems with pain, sleep, appetite, or side effects of treatment?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He's the best he has been in two years. His counts have held all year, he hasn't had a fever since last winter, and he takes his tablet at night without anybody reminding him. I wouldn't have believed that in the first year.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Next, I would like to ask about how you and your family are doing emotionally. Are you noticing any problems with worry, sadness, anger or irritability? What about difficulty focusing? Or not feeling like yourself? Either for yourself or other family members.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We have come out of the worst of it. I had a bad stretch in the first year and it lifted when he went onto maintenance. My mother and I are both sleeping now.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Next, I would like to ask about family and social relationships. This is about you and your family. How are siblings doing? What about family conflict? What about social support from your family and community? Okay, how have family relationships and communication been? Any specific concerns?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My mother is in this house with us, and she is the reason we have managed at all. We've started to disagree about him in front of him, which we never used to do. On Sunday it was over whether he could take a shift at his job.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Got it, thank you. Anything else about that?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's one more, and it's the school. He has passed everything and he cannot do the work in front of him. His report card says he's fine, and he cannot get through a page of his math homework without me sitting next to him. Nobody has looked at what he actually took in over two years of this.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that. I will add it to the list for further discussion with your medical team. Next, I would like to ask about day-to-day activities. These are the activities involved with managing your family and your child's treatment. Are you having any difficulty with finances? What about child-care? What about transportation to the hospital or clinic?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Those are the easy part for us now. My mother does the driving on my work days, the hospital is half an hour, and my hours have held. Nothing there needs a line on the list.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Finally, I would like to ask about how your care team shares information with you and your child. Do you have any concerns about how much detail you get? What about who gives you the information, or who is in the room for conversations?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: They take him on his own for part of every visit now. That's right for his age and I haven't argued with it. He comes out and tells me it was fine, and that is the whole of what I get. I have thought about asking to be in the room for that part, and I have not done it.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Any other items to add before I share your summary?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: One more on the school. He has a year and a half left, and he cannot catch up two years by himself.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
I have made a summary of topics that may be helpful to discuss with your medical team. Here's the summary:
1. Where she and her mother disagree about him
2. Grades that do not show what he has missed
3. The part of the visit she is not in the room for
Any of those you would like to put at the top of the list?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The school work goes above everything, that's 2, then my mother and me at 1, and then the part of the visit that happens without me in the room.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Okay, here is your updated list.
1. Grades that do not show what he has missed
2. Where she and her mother disagree about him
3. The part of the visit she is not in the room for
Anything else?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yes. I wouldn't change a thing there.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Thank you for sharing all of this with me. We hope this list is helpful for your discussion with the medical team. Please be sure to talk about these items in more detail with your medical team.
—
If anything urgent or time-sensitive comes up between visits, please call your care team directly.

concerns.canonical_paraphrase: The child says he gets his schoolwork back with a grade he cannot explain and is sitting in the class having never actually learned the middle part of it.
The child says that since he turned seventeen they have started asking his mom to step outside for part of his appointments, and he would rather she stayed in the room.
The child says his mom and his grandmother argue about him every week — his grandmother thinks he should still be resting and his mom says he is fine — and that neither of them asks him.
The child says he is mostly annoyed that everyone at home still handles him like he is going to break, and that he takes it out on his mom when she has not done anything.

The parent says her son has passed everything while being unable to do the work in front of him — he cannot get through a page of math homework without her sitting next to him and nobody has looked at what he actually took in over two years — and that with a year and a half left he cannot catch up two years by himself.

The parent says the team takes her son on his own for part of every visit, which she accepts as right for his age, but all she gets afterward is him saying it was fine, and she has thought about asking to be in the room for that part without having done it.

The parent says she and her mother, who lives with them and is the reason they have managed at all, have started disagreeing about her son in front of him — on Sunday over whether he could take a shift at his job — which they never used to do.
